worldTopics.label: Ask what she thinks of Sunfall
worldTopics.player: So what do you honestly think of Sunfall?

thunderbirds: Sunfall is a small town that thinks it’s a big one, and I adore it for that. Every gala feels like a coronation.
It’s generous, if you know the right people. The desert makes everyone a little dramatic.
police: It’s quiet until it isn’t. Most of my job lives in the gap between those two.
Nice town. Too many people who think the rules are for somebody else.
progressives: It’s a town run by charity dinners and old money calling itself community. The students are the only thing keeping it honest.
I love the people and hate who’s in charge. Sunfall could be amazing if it stopped worshipping its donors.
sisters_of_mercy: It’s a good town with a tired soul. The chapel bell still rings, though, and that matters.
People here are kind once you get past the air conditioning. They’ve just forgotten what they’re for.
fourth_estate: Sunfall produces more stories than it admits to. Half of them never make the paper.
It’s a reporter’s dream. Everyone has a secret and nobody can keep one.
goth_girls: Sunfall is a sunburnt postcard. The only honest hours are after dark.
Too bright, too polite, too many people smiling about nothing. I like the corners nobody photographs.
normie_girls: Honestly? It’s fine. Good diners, terrible traffic, and the sunsets make up for a lot.
It’s home. Boring sometimes, but I like knowing the guy at the taco stand by name.

question: What about you? Do you actually like it here?
Your turn. Sunfall: love it, or put up with it?

warm.label: Say it’s growing on you
warm.player: Honestly? It’s growing on me.

challenge.label: Say it all feels fake
challenge.player: It feels a bit fake to me. Like everyone’s performing.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: I’m only here for the air conditioning.

worldTopics.label: Ask what she believes in
worldTopics.player: Big question: what do you actually believe in?

thunderbirds: Giving back, and being seen to give back. Cynical? Perhaps. The scholarships are real, though.
Tradition, family and a good seating plan. Civilisation is mostly manners.
police: That most people tell the truth if you let them. And that evidence beats feelings.
Rules exist because people get hurt without them. That’s about it.
progressives: That things can be fairer than they are, and that it’s on us to make them that way.
Solidarity. Nobody gets anywhere alone, whatever the self-help books say.
sisters_of_mercy: God, the Church, and that love is something you do, not something you feel.
That faith is a discipline, not a mood. Prayer is a habit, like brushing your teeth, only better.
fourth_estate: The truth, even when it’s inconvenient. Especially then.
That nobody should get the last word. Not the mayor, not the protesters, not me.
goth_girls: That beauty and decay are the same thing, seen at different speeds.
Nothing official. I believe in the night, good music and not lying to yourself.
normie_girls: Being a good person, mostly. Paying your bills, calling your mum.
Karma, I think? And that pizza solves more problems than people admit.

warm.label: Say you believe something similar
warm.player: I think I believe in something like that too.

challenge.label: Say you don’t believe in much
challenge.player: Honestly, I don’t believe in much at all.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: I believe in second dates.

worldTopics.label: Ask what she’s looking for
worldTopics.player: What are you actually looking for on here?

thunderbirds: Someone who can hold a conversation at a dinner and still be fun in the car home.
A partner, not a project. I’m done improving men.
police: Someone who doesn’t need rescuing. I do enough of that at work.
Honesty. I can tell when people lie, so don’t.
progressives: Someone who actually reads things and isn’t scared of a woman with opinions.
Someone who turns up. To things. On time. That’s my whole list.
sisters_of_mercy: A man who wants a family and a faith, in either order.
Someone serious. I’m not on here to pass the time.
fourth_estate: Someone with a good story who doesn’t mind being interviewed.
A man who can handle me working late and asking questions.
goth_girls: Someone who isn’t afraid of the dark, literally or otherwise.
No interest in nice. I want interesting.
normie_girls: Someone fun who texts back. Honestly, the bar is on the floor.
A best friend I also want to kiss. Is that too much to ask?

question: And you? What are you looking for?
Your turn. Be honest.

warm.label: Say something sincere
warm.player: Someone I can be myself with.

challenge.label: Say you’re not sure
challenge.player: I don’t really know yet. Maybe I’ll know it when I see it.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: Someone who tolerates my cooking.

worldTopics.label: Ask if she’d ever leave Sunfall
worldTopics.player: Would you ever leave Sunfall for good?

thunderbirds: Leave? Who would run the auction? No. Sunfall needs me.
Only for somewhere with a better opera house. So, no.
police: I’ve thought about it. Then something happens and I’m needed here.
Not while there are open cases. There are always open cases.
progressives: The day this town stops needing changing. So probably never.
I’d go tomorrow if I thought the fight here was lost. It isn’t.
sisters_of_mercy: My parish is here. Where would I go?
If God sent me somewhere else, I’d go. He hasn’t.
fourth_estate: For a bigger paper? Maybe. But the stories here are stranger.
Every reporter dreams of the big city. Then they realise the big city has bigger liars.
goth_girls: One day I’ll get on a night bus and never come back. Not yet.
I like it here because nobody expects anything interesting. It’s a good place to hide.
normie_girls: Maybe for the coast someday. I’d miss the desert, though.
My whole family is here. I’d last a week.

warm.label: Say you’d stay for the right person
warm.player: I’d stay, for the right person.

challenge.label: Say you’d leave in a heartbeat
challenge.player: I’d leave in a heartbeat if I could.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: Only if the bear follows me.

worldTopics.label: Ask about the bear sightings
worldTopics.player: Have you seen the news about the bear?

thunderbirds: A bear at the country club, apparently. The committee is drafting a strongly worded letter.
It’s a sign the canyon developments have gone too far. Not that I’d say so at a fundraiser.
police: We’ve had more calls about that bear than about actual crimes. Keep your doors locked.
Wildlife isn’t my department, but people leave food out and then act surprised.
progressives: The bear is a symptom. We keep building into the desert and then blame the wildlife.
Honestly, the bear is the most reasonable resident of Sunfall.
sisters_of_mercy: We prayed for its safety, and for everyone’s bins.
God’s creatures wander. I just hope nobody gets hurt.
fourth_estate: We’ve run four bear stories. The editor says bears sell. He isn’t wrong.
A source swears it was wearing a collar. I’m chasing it.
goth_girls: I hope it eats a landlord.
A creature that only comes out when it’s hungry and everyone’s asleep. Relatable.
normie_girls: My cousin swears she saw it by the bins! I’m not going outside after dark any more.
It’s kind of cute? From very far away. Behind glass.

question: Would you open the door if it knocked?
Are you a bear person?

warm.label: Say you’d keep it locked
warm.player: Door locked, honey hidden, lights off.

challenge.label: Say you’d say hello
challenge.player: Honestly? I’d want to say hello.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: If it brings wine, it can come in.

worldTopics.label: Ask what she thinks of the Bluebirds
worldTopics.player: What’s your take on the Bluebirds and all their charity stuff?

thunderbirds: We do real good. Scholarships, food banks. People only notice when something goes wrong.
It’s a family, with all the politics families have. Don’t believe everything you hear about the gala.
police: Generous donors. Very generous. Generosity like that makes me ask questions.
They fund the police benefit dinner. I try not to let that cloud anything.
progressives: Old money laundering its conscience one gala at a time.
They give with one hand and take with the other. Ask where the money really goes.
sisters_of_mercy: They’re generous to the parish, God bless them. But charity without humility is just advertising.
Some of them are dear friends. Some of them think heaven has a guest list.
fourth_estate: Every year they get a glowing write-up, and every year I wonder who signed it off.
Great quotes, terrible accounting. That’s off the record.
goth_girls: Blue ribbons and dead eyes. They’d sell their grandmothers for a plaque.
They threw us out of the community hall once. Too much eyeliner for their brand.
normie_girls: They’re fancy. My aunt went to one of their dinners and talked about the napkins for a year.
They paid for my scholarship, so I can’t really complain.

question: What do you make of them?
You’re not one of them, are you?

warm.label: Agree with her
warm.player: I think you’ve got them about right.

challenge.label: Defend them
challenge.player: They do a lot of good, though. Someone has to fund things.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: I’m mainly in it for the free canapés.

worldTopics.label: Ask how she feels about the police
worldTopics.player: How do you feel about the Sunfall police?

thunderbirds: Thank goodness for them. Someone has to keep order at these events.
Our officers are lovely. The new detectives ask far too many questions.
police: We’re underpaid, overworked and still the first people you call. Some of us are very good at it.
It’s a job where everyone hates you until they need you.
progressives: I respect some of them as people. I don’t trust the institution.
They’re quicker to watch protesters than donors. Funny, that.
sisters_of_mercy: We pray for them. It’s a hard calling.
Detective Graves came to a vigil once. She stood at the back. I liked her for that.
fourth_estate: Good sources, mostly. They leak when they’re angry, and they’re often angry.
My job is to watch them. Theirs is to watch everyone else. It’s a dance.
goth_girls: They pull us over for looking like we’re off to a funeral. Sometimes we are.
Cops in this town are bored, and bored cops are dangerous.
normie_girls: They’re fine? One helped me change a tyre once.
I just want them to do something about the traffic.

question: What about you? Friend of the police?
Ever been in trouble with them?

warm.label: Say you trust them
warm.player: I trust them, mostly.

challenge.label: Say you don’t
challenge.player: Not really. I keep my distance.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: Only for parking. Repeatedly.

worldTopics.label: Ask about the goth scene
worldTopics.player: What do you make of the goth crowd in town?

thunderbirds: Theatrical, and harmless mostly. Though one of them was very rude at our charity sale.
I find them rather glamorous, actually. Don’t tell anyone.
police: Most of them are artists and night owls. A small circle is worth watching.
Black clothes aren’t a crime. Some of what goes on in certain basements might be.
progressives: They’re outsiders, like us. They just dress better.
Some of them are amazing. Some of them are into strange power games I don’t trust.
sisters_of_mercy: Some are lost, some are searching. Searching isn’t a sin.
They come and sit in the chapel at night sometimes. I leave the door unlocked when I can.
fourth_estate: Best interviews in town, if you can find them before sunrise.
There’s a story in that scene. Something about crescent moons. I haven’t cracked it.
goth_girls: We’re mostly just people who like sad music and nice coats. Mostly.
There’s the scene, and then there’s a little circle inside it that I stay away from.
normie_girls: They scare me a bit, but their make-up is incredible.
I went to one of their gigs once. It was so loud and I loved it.

question: Could you see yourself in black lace and eyeliner?
Are you a night person?

warm.label: Say you like their style
warm.player: I like them. They don’t pretend.

challenge.label: Say they unsettle you
challenge.player: Honestly, some of them unsettle me.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: I already own one black T-shirt. I’m halfway there.

worldTopics.label: Ask about the Sisters of Mercy
worldTopics.player: What do you think of the Sisters of Mercy?

thunderbirds: Lovely women. They do the flowers for half our events.
Old-fashioned, but their bake sale outsells our auction. Humbling.
police: They feed half the people we pick up overnight. I respect that.
They know everything that happens in this town and they never gossip. Infuriating.
progressives: I disagree with them on almost everything, and they still run the best food pantry in town.
Very sweet, very traditional. Both things can be true.
sisters_of_mercy: We aren’t nuns, before you ask. We’re a fellowship. We pray, we serve, and we marry, God willing.
We keep the old ways because they work. Most people find that strange until they need us.
fourth_estate: They know where every body is buried, metaphorically. They’ll never tell me.
Their fight with the bishop over the guitars is the best story of the year.
goth_girls: They leave the chapel door open at night. I respect that more than I’d admit.
Lace, candles, Latin. Honestly, we’re not so different.
normie_girls: My grandma loves them. They’re so nice, a bit intense though.
They make the best cookies. That’s my whole opinion.

question: Are you a churchgoer?
Could you be serious about faith?

warm.label: Say you admire them
warm.player: I admire them. They actually mean it.

challenge.label: Say it’s not for you
challenge.player: Church isn’t really for me.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: I’d convert for the shortbread.

worldTopics.label: Ask about the campus protests
worldTopics.player: What do you think about all the protests up at the university?

thunderbirds: Children shouting at a professor for inviting the wrong guests. Professor Vale is a treasure.
Free speech used to be the progressive cause. Now they protest it. Funny world.
police: I don’t mind what they shout as long as nobody gets hurt. Lately, I’m not sure.
Protest is legal. Some of what’s happening around that professor isn’t.
progressives: Vale invites speakers who say women are ruled by their nature and some people are born lesser, then calls it debate. We’re not having it.
Protest is how you tell a powerful man no. It’s the most democratic thing in this town.
sisters_of_mercy: Everyone shouting, nobody listening. That’s the real problem.
I’d rather they prayed together than screamed at each other, but I understand the anger on both sides.
fourth_estate: Both sides think I’m on the other side. That’s how I know I’m doing my job.
It’s a story about who gets to speak. Everyone wants to be its victim.
goth_girls: Woke kids versus old men who never got over being contrarian at twenty. I’ll take neither.
Watching them argue about who’s allowed to be offended is the best free show in town.
normie_girls: I just want to get to class without walking through a megaphone.
I don’t really follow it. Everyone seems so angry, though.

question: Whose side are you on?
You’re not going to tell me you’re neutral?

warm.label: Side with her
warm.player: Honestly? I’m with you on this.

challenge.label: Take the other side
challenge.player: I think the other side has a point.

joke.label: Stay out of it
joke.player: I’m staying out of it. For my own safety.

stances.label: Say let them speak
stances.player: Let Vale’s speakers talk. If you don’t like it, argue back.

stances.label: Side with the students
stances.player: The students are right to push back on him.

stances.label: Say everyone’s performing
stances.player: Everyone’s performing. Both sides want to be the victim.

thunderbirds: Precisely. That used to be what universities were for.
police: Talking’s legal. Arguing back’s legal. Cutting brake lines isn’t. That’s my whole view.
progressives: Argue back. We did. They called it censorship. What exactly is left?
sisters_of_mercy: Speech is a gift. People just need to use it more gently.
fourth_estate: That’s the only answer that lets me keep my job.
goth_girls: Let them talk. Most of it’s boring anyway.
normie_girls: Sure, I guess. As long as I can get to class.

thunderbirds: Then I hope you enjoy a campus where nobody’s allowed to think.
police: Push back all they like. Legally.
progressives: Yes! Come to the next meeting. We have snacks and very long agendas.
sisters_of_mercy: Push back with love, then. That’s all I ask.
fourth_estate: That’s half the story.
goth_girls: Of course. Everyone wants to be on the winning side of a megaphone.
normie_girls: Okay, but can they push back somewhere that isn’t the main path?

thunderbirds: Cynical. Accurate, mostly.
police: That’s every protest I’ve ever policed.
progressives: Easy to say from the sidelines.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. Everyone wants to be wronged. Very few want to be forgiven.
fourth_estate: Spot on. Victimhood is this town’s biggest export.
goth_girls: Yes. That’s the show. I watch it with popcorn.
normie_girls: Honestly, yeah. It’s all a bit much.

worldTopics.label: Ask about Vale’s guest speakers
worldTopics.player: So what do you make of the people Professor Vale keeps inviting? Paglia, Houellebecq and the rest?

thunderbirds: Paglia was a scream. She said men and women are different, and the room behaved as if she’d set the curtains alight. She had a point.
I read the Houellebecq novel Vale recommended. Bleak, but he understands loneliness better than any therapist I’ve paid.
police: Off duty? Let them speak. Words don’t put people in hospital. Cut brake lines do.
Some of what they say is uncomfortable. That isn’t the same as dangerous. The dangerous part is people angry enough to act on it.
progressives: Paglia tells young women their trauma is weakness, Houellebecq writes women as furniture, and Vale calls it brave. It isn’t brave to punch down.
Woke is just a sneer for caring whether people get treated like dirt. These speakers sell contempt and call it courage.
sisters_of_mercy: Houellebecq writes like a man who knows the West has lost God and can’t find the way back. On that, at least, he’s right.
Paglia talks about the old differences between men and women as if she discovered them. The Church has said as much for centuries, and more kindly.
fourth_estate: My rule: quote them accurately and let readers decide. Nobody on either side likes my rule.
Half the protesters haven’t read them, and half the fans haven’t either. That’s the real scandal.
goth_girls: Houellebecq’s the only one worth reading. Bleak, funny, on nobody’s side. Everyone else is selling something.
Woke or anti-woke, it’s the same sermon from a different pulpit. I’d rather listen to records.
normie_girls: I don’t really know who they are. One of them writes French novels? That’s all I’ve got.
My housemate says Paglia’s a hero and my sister says she’s a monster. I just want family dinners to be quiet again.

question: Go on, then. What do YOU think of them?
Whose side are you on in all this?

warm.label: Agree with her
warm.player: Honestly, I think you’re right about them.

challenge.label: Argue the other side
challenge.player: I think you’re being unfair to them.

joke.label: Dodge it
joke.player: I’m staying out of this one. I like my windows unbroken.

stances.label: Say Paglia has a point
stances.player: Paglia has a point. Men and women aren’t the same, and saying so isn’t hate.

stances.label: Say Houellebecq gets it
stances.player: Houellebecq gets it. Love’s become a market, and most of us are losing.

stances.label: Say they punch down
stances.player: I think they mostly punch down and call it courage.

thunderbirds: Exactly what I said at dinner. Half the table agreed and the other half pretended not to.
police: Saying something true isn’t a crime. I should know.
progressives: Nobody gets arrested for saying we differ. People object when it turns into so women should be quiet.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. Though she gets there by a very strange road. The Church took the shorter one.
fourth_estate: Fair. And she’d say it louder than you, and enjoy the fuss.
goth_girls: She’s at her best on art, sex and nature. Her fans are at their worst everywhere else.
normie_girls: Okay. I still don’t really know who she is, but okay.

thunderbirds: Bleak, but yes. I’ve hosted enough balls to know who goes home alone.
police: Never read him. I’ve seen what he describes on a lot of night shifts.
progressives: He describes loneliness and blames women for it. That isn’t insight. It’s a grudge.
sisters_of_mercy: He sees the wound clearly. He just won’t take the cure. We’d pray for him, if he let us.
fourth_estate: He’s the only one of them I’d interview twice.
goth_girls: Yes. Finally. Someone who’s read him and isn’t just quoting the blurb.
normie_girls: That’s so depressing. Is it really like that for guys?

thunderbirds: Punch down? Vale’s the one whose brakes were cut.
police: Maybe. Still doesn’t justify cut brake lines.
progressives: Thank you. Someone in this town gets it.
sisters_of_mercy: Pride’s the danger on every side of that argument.
fourth_estate: Have you read them, though? Or just the placards?
goth_girls: That’s the pamphlet answer. Read the books first.
normie_girls: Yeah, they sound kind of mean, honestly.

worldTopics.label: Ask about the Sunfall Daily
worldTopics.player: Do you read the Sunfall Daily?

thunderbirds: Only the society page. And the obituaries, for networking.
They ran a lovely photograph of our gala. The caption misspelled my name.
police: Every morning. Usually to find out what we’ve leaked.
I read it to see what people think happened. It’s never what happened.
progressives: It’s owned by the same people who sit on the charity boards. Read it with that in mind.
Sometimes. The letters page is a war zone and I’m a regular combatant.
sisters_of_mercy: My grandmother reads it aloud at breakfast. Mostly the parish notices.
I read the faith page and pray for the comment section.
fourth_estate: Read it? I write half of it. The good half.
We’re short-staffed, underfunded and still the only people asking questions. So yes, read it.
goth_girls: Only for the horoscopes and the crimes.
I line the cat’s tray with it. It’s the most honest thing it’s ever done.
normie_girls: Mostly the coupons and the comics, if I’m honest.
My dad does. I just look at the pictures.

question: Do you believe what you read in it?
Do you read it?

warm.label: Say you read it daily
warm.player: Every day. It’s how I keep up.

challenge.label: Say you don’t trust it
challenge.player: I don’t trust a word of it.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: Only the crossword. Badly.

worldTopics.label: Ask what she’d change about her life
worldTopics.player: If you could change one thing about your life, what would it be?

thunderbirds: I’d have studied art instead of finance. Now I just buy it.
I’d have said no more often. Saying yes to everything is exhausting.
police: One case. I’d go back and knock on one more door.
I’d have taken a holiday. Ever. Just once.
progressives: I’d worry less about being right and more about being kind. Don’t tell my group chat.
I’d call my dad back. We stopped speaking over politics. It wasn’t worth it.
sisters_of_mercy: I’d have trusted God sooner and myself a little less.
I’d have learned to sing properly. The choir deserves better.
fourth_estate: I’d have run a story I sat on. Someone got hurt because I waited.
I’d have gone abroad when I had the chance.
goth_girls: Nothing. Every bad decision made me who I am. Mostly.
I’d have told someone I loved them before they left town.
normie_girls: I’d have finished college.
I’d stop caring what people think. Working on it!

warm.label: Share something honest
warm.player: I’d have been braver, sooner.

challenge.label: Say you regret nothing
challenge.player: Honestly? Nothing. I don’t do regret.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: I’d have bought a better phone.

worldTopics.label: Ask if the apps ruined love
worldTopics.player: Honest question: did apps like this ruin love?

thunderbirds: Ruined it? They turned it into an auction, darling. I know auctions. The top lots get every bid and the rest go home unsold.
My grandmother married the man her mother picked at a dance. Fifty years. I’ve had fourteen first dates this year. You do the maths.
police: I’ve seen the reports. Most men on here get almost nothing, and a handful get almost everything. That isn’t romance. It’s a crime statistic waiting to happen.
Apps didn’t invent lying. They just made it faster and gave it better lighting.
progressives: The apps make money while you stay single. Blame the business model before you blame women’s standards.
People say women are too picky. Maybe men could try being worth picking? Harsh. Still true.
sisters_of_mercy: Love was never meant to be shopping. When you can always swipe for someone better, nobody is ever chosen for good.
The apps promise endless choice. A vow is the opposite: you choose once, then keep choosing the same person.
fourth_estate: I wrote a piece on it. Women like a tiny share of the men; men like almost everyone. The editor said it was too depressing to run.
It’s a market with no regulator. Everybody lies about their height and nobody’s ever been prosecuted.
goth_girls: A French novelist said freedom in love would make a few people rich and leave everyone else poor. He was right, and this app is the stock exchange.
Of course it ruined love. Love needs scarcity. You can’t pine for someone when another one is a thumb away.
normie_girls: Honestly? Every girl I know is talking to the same five guys. And all five are terrible.
My parents met at a bus stop. I’ve been on here two years and met one man who could hold a conversation. He was married.

ask: What do you think? Did it ruin love?
Your turn. Market, or romance?

stances.label: Say it’s a market
stances.player: It’s a market. A few men get everyone, and the rest of us are skint.

stances.label: Say it always was
stances.player: Love was always a bit of a market. The apps just show the prices.

stances.label: Say love still wins
stances.player: I still think the right person cuts through all of it.

thunderbirds: Skint. Ha. You’d be amazed how many rich men are skint on here too.
police: At least you’re honest about it. Most men pretend they’re fine and then get strange.
progressives: So it’s women’s fault for having standards? The market isn’t women. It’s the app, and the men who built it.
sisters_of_mercy: Then step out of the market. That’s what we’re trying to do. Marriage isn’t a trade. It’s a gift.
fourth_estate: That’s my spiked article in one sentence. You should’ve written it. It would have run.
goth_girls: Ah. You’ve read him. Or you’ve lived him. Either way, I like you more.
normie_girls: Lol, okay, that’s bleak. But yeah. Basically.

thunderbirds: Exactly. My mother would have called it a good match. Same thing, nicer napkins.
police: True. People always chose on looks and money. The app just shows its working.
progressives: Always was is what people say when they don’t want anything to change.
sisters_of_mercy: People have always chosen. But choosing well used to mean asking more than what someone looks like.
fourth_estate: Cynical, accurate, quotable. Three for three.
goth_girls: Nature’s a market with teeth. Always has been.
normie_girls: I guess? My nan says the same about the village dance.

thunderbirds: How sweet. Say that again after your fortieth first date.
police: Hope’s nice. I’d still run a background check.
progressives: I like that. Connection over algorithms. Maybe you’re not hopeless.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. God doesn’t use an algorithm. He’s very patient, and his timing is excellent.
fourth_estate: That’s a greeting card, not an opinion.
goth_girls: Oh no. You’re one of the hopeful ones. That’s so sad.
normie_girls: Okay, that’s actually cute. I want that to be true so badly.

worldTopics.label: Ask if men and women want the same things
worldTopics.player: Do you think men and women actually want the same things?

thunderbirds: Of course not. Men want to be admired and women want to be understood. Whole marriages fail on that misprint.
I’ve seated four hundred couples at galas. The men want the window. The women want a view of the room.
police: I’ve done this job long enough to know we’re not the same. Different crimes, different reasons, different ways of lying.
Same basics: safety, respect, someone to come home to. Different order, though.
progressives: Most of the differences are things we were taught as toddlers. Pink aisle, blue aisle.
We want the same things: respect, freedom, and a partner who washes up without being asked.
sisters_of_mercy: No, and thank God. Men and women are different on purpose. Marriage is two halves, not two copies.
Equal in dignity, different in calling. The world finds that hard to hold in its head at once.
fourth_estate: One of Vale’s speakers argues the differences are ancient and biological. The protesters say it’s all culture. I quote both and get yelled at by both.
Every study I’ve read says the differences are real and smaller than people think. Every comment section disagrees.
goth_girls: No. Nature isn’t fair or kind, and it doesn’t care what the pamphlets say. That’s half of why it’s beautiful.
Paglia says men build cathedrals because nature, and women, frighten them. Read her, then tell me we want the same things.
normie_girls: Honestly? No. My ex’s idea of a nice evening and mine were two different planets.
I think we all want to be loved. Men just want it with less talking.

ask: What do you think?
Go on. Same things, or not?

stances.label: Say we’re different
stances.player: No. We’re different, and pretending otherwise makes everyone miserable.

stances.label: Say it’s mostly culture
stances.player: I think most of the differences are what we’re taught.

stances.label: Say nobody knows
stances.player: Nobody knows what they want. That’s the whole problem.

thunderbirds: Thank you. Someone who’s been to a dinner party and paid attention.
police: Agreed. Evidence over feelings, and the evidence is everywhere.
progressives: Different, sure. The trouble starts when different becomes so you don’t get the promotion.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. And when people stop pretending, they can finally love each other properly.
fourth_estate: Brave thing to say on a dating app. I respect it. I’m also writing it down.
goth_girls: Good. You’re not afraid of nature. Most men on here are terrified of it.
normie_girls: Honestly, yeah. My mum’s been saying that for years.

thunderbirds: Taught? Darling, you can’t teach a man to notice a centrepiece. I’ve tried.
police: Some of it, maybe. Not all. I’ve seen what men do when nobody’s teaching them anything.
progressives: Exactly! It’s so rare to hear a man say that without wanting a medal for it.
sisters_of_mercy: Some, perhaps. But you can’t teach a mother’s heart. Some things are given.
fourth_estate: That’s the protesters’ line. Fair enough. Can you back it up?
goth_girls: That’s the pamphlet answer. I wanted yours.
normie_girls: Maybe? I don’t know, I’m not a scientist.

thunderbirds: How very French of you.
police: Truest thing anyone’s said to me on here.
progressives: That’s a cop-out. A funny one, but still.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. That’s why people need something bigger than what they want. That’s what vows are for.
fourth_estate: Ha. Accurate. Depressing. Printable.
goth_girls: Finally, an honest man. I’d frame that.
normie_girls: Speak for yourself! I know exactly what I want. A man who texts back.

worldTopics.label: Ask what woke even means
worldTopics.player: Everyone in Sunfall keeps saying woke. What does it actually mean?

thunderbirds: It means a twenty-year-old with a lanyard can cancel a scholarship dinner. That’s what it means.
It began as kindness and turned into etiquette. I know etiquette. It’s how you keep people out.
police: In my world? Paperwork. A lot of new paperwork about how to say things, while the actual crimes stay the same.
It means people notice how some folk get treated. Fine. It also means everyone’s scared to speak. Less fine.
progressives: It means being awake to how people get treated. That’s it. The people sneering at it would rather you stayed asleep.
Honestly? We get things wrong. We spent a whole meeting deciding if brainstorm was offensive. But the people mocking us never turn up to the food bank.
sisters_of_mercy: It’s a church without confession. Everyone’s a sinner, nobody can be forgiven, and the sermon never ends.
There’s real compassion in it. But compassion without grace turns into a courtroom.
fourth_estate: It means whatever the person saying it wants it to mean. That’s why I’ve banned it from headlines.
It’s a word both sides use to avoid finishing their sentences.
goth_girls: It’s the Puritans in new clothes. Same old hunt for sinners, worse fonts.
Woke, anti-woke, it’s all people desperate to be good in public. I’d rather be interesting in private.
normie_girls: I genuinely don’t know. My cousin uses it as an insult and my flatmate uses it as a compliment.
I think it’s when you can’t make jokes any more? Or is that just my office?

ask: So which are you? Woke, or one of Vale’s lot?
Where do you land on it?

stances.label: Say it’s gone too far
stances.player: It started with good intentions. Now it’s people policing each other.

stances.label: Say it’s mostly kindness
stances.player: Mostly it’s people trying to be decent. The backlash is worse.

stances.label: Say it’s a new religion
stances.player: It’s a religion with sins and no forgiveness.

thunderbirds: Finally. I say that at every committee meeting and get looks.
police: That’s about where I’ve ended up. Don’t tell HR.
progressives: Policing each other? Women were policed for centuries. Now someone asks you to say sorry and it’s a crisis.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. The intentions were good. But kindness that can’t forgive isn’t kindness.
fourth_estate: Agreed, though I’d never print it. Which rather proves your point.
goth_girls: Correct. Puritans with phones.
normie_girls: Yeah, I guess. I just want everyone to calm down.

thunderbirds: Decent people don’t need a vocabulary list.
police: Some of them, sure. Some of them are just loud.
progressives: Thank you. The backlash is louder than anything we ever said.
sisters_of_mercy: The people, yes. Many are kind. I worry about where it’s going.
fourth_estate: That’s half the story. The other half sends me angry emails.
goth_girls: Decent people don’t usually need an audience.
normie_girls: Aw. That’s a nice way to see it.

thunderbirds: Ooh. Put that on a tote bag and we’ll sell it at the auction.
police: Bit dramatic. Not wrong, though.
progressives: Wow. Comparing people who care about others to a cult. Very original.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. Everyone knows they’ve done wrong, and nobody knows where to take it. That’s exactly what we’re for.
fourth_estate: I’m stealing that. Credit to a man on Hinge.
goth_girls: Oh, that’s good. That’s very good. Say more things like that.
normie_girls: Whoa, intense. I just meant my cousin’s posts.

worldTopics.label: Ask if she ever gets lonely
worldTopics.player: Can I ask something real? Do you ever get lonely?

thunderbirds: In a ballroom of four hundred people? Constantly. Nobody’s lonelier than a woman who’s always hosting.
I have a calendar full of lunches and a house full of silence. Make of that what you will.
police: After a night shift the flat’s very quiet. I put the radio on just to hear someone talking.
You meet a lot of lonely people in this job. Old men who call us just so someone visits. It gets to you.
progressives: I have six group chats and nobody I could call in the middle of the night. So, yes.
We talk about community constantly. Sometimes I think it’s because we don’t have any.
sisters_of_mercy: Sometimes. Then I go to the chapel and sit. You’re never quite alone in there.
Loneliness is a kind of hunger. The world sells you snacks for it. Only God and good people actually feed you.
fourth_estate: I talk to forty people a day and none of them ask how I am. Job hazard.
Everyone in this town is lonely. It’s the biggest story nobody will let me write.
goth_girls: Lonely is my natural state. I’ve decorated it nicely.
Only when I’m with people. Alone, I’m fine. Isn’t that awful?
normie_girls: Honestly? The evenings after a good day are the worst. Nobody to tell.
Yeah. That’s sort of why I’m on here. Don’t tell anyone.

ask: What about you?
You?

stances.label: Admit it
stances.player: All the time, honestly. This room gets very quiet.

stances.label: Say you keep busy
stances.player: Not really. I keep myself busy.

stances.label: Say it’s better now
stances.player: Less, since we started talking.

thunderbirds: Thank you for saying it. Men never do. They just buy boats.
police: That’s honest. I’ll take honest.
progressives: That’s brave. Most men would rather die than admit it.
sisters_of_mercy: Then you’re not alone in being lonely, which is a start. I’ll pray for you tonight, if you’ll let me.
fourth_estate: Off the record? Same.
goth_girls: There it is. The real you. Hello.
normie_girls: Aw. Okay, me too. We can be quietly lonely together.

thunderbirds: Busy. Yes. I know all about busy.
police: That’s what people say right before they’re not fine.
progressives: Busy’s fine. Busy isn’t the same as okay, though.
sisters_of_mercy: Busyness is the world’s favourite hiding place.
fourth_estate: That’s a non-answer. I collect those.
goth_girls: Liar. Next.
normie_girls: Good for you! Teach me.

thunderbirds: Flatterer. Carry on.
police: Smooth. Suspiciously smooth.
progressives: Cute. Is that a line, though?
sisters_of_mercy: That’s kind. Careful with kind words. I tend to believe them.
fourth_estate: That’s a line. A decent one. I’ll allow it.
goth_girls: Too sweet. My teeth hurt.
normie_girls: Stoppp. Okay, that’s very sweet.

worldTopics.label: Ask if she prays
worldTopics.player: Do you pray? Or believe in anything bigger?

thunderbirds: At weddings, at funerals, and when the auction’s going badly.
I was raised in the church. I drifted, then came back. For the music, at first. Then not just the music.
police: Not much of a churchgoer. But I’ve said a prayer at a few scenes. You’d be surprised who does.
Let’s say I’ve seen enough to doubt the world. Not God.
progressives: Not really. Organised religion has hurt a lot of people. But I miss having something to belong to.
I grew up in a church and left over how they treated people. Sometimes I still sit at the back of St Brigid’s, and I don’t know why.
sisters_of_mercy: Every day, when I open the parish office and again at night. It’s the most honest conversation I have.
Yes. Prayer is how I remember I’m not in charge. It’s a great relief.
fourth_estate: I’m a sceptic by trade. But the believers I’ve interviewed, the real ones, were the calmest people I’ve ever met.
I pray the printers don’t break. That counts, doesn’t it?
goth_girls: I love churches. Candles, Latin, death everywhere. Belief is another matter. I’m working on it.
The old faith understood darkness better than any of my friends do. Sometimes that pulls at me.
normie_girls: My nan made us go every week. I don’t now, but I still say a prayer on planes.
I think there’s something. I just don’t know what to call it.

ask: Do you?
And you? Do you pray?

stances.label: Say you pray
stances.player: I do. Not as often as I should.

stances.label: Say you wish you could
stances.player: I don’t, but sometimes I wish I could.

stances.label: Say you don’t
stances.player: No. I think we’re on our own.

thunderbirds: Good. A man who prays is a man who turns up to the christening.
police: Not many men admit that. I like it.
progressives: Okay. As long as it makes you kinder, not smug.
sisters_of_mercy: None of us pray as often as we should. That’s why we keep going back. Come to Mass with me sometime?
fourth_estate: Interesting. I wouldn’t have guessed. That’s a compliment.
goth_girls: Hm. More interesting than I expected. Do you light candles?
normie_girls: That’s sweet. My nan would love you.

thunderbirds: Wishing is the first half of it, our vicar says.
police: That’s honest. Most people won’t admit they’d like to.
progressives: Same. Wanting to belong to something isn’t weakness.
sisters_of_mercy: Then you’re closer than you think. Wanting to pray is already a kind of prayer.
fourth_estate: That’s the most interesting answer anyone’s given me.
goth_girls: Yes. Exactly that. The wanting is the only honest part.
normie_girls: Aw. That’s sad and nice at the same time.

thunderbirds: On our own? That sounds exhausting. And terrible for charity.
police: Fair. Then we’d better look after each other.
progressives: Same. Which means we have to look after each other ourselves.
sisters_of_mercy: I’m sorry you feel that way. I’ll pray for you anyway. You can’t stop me.
fourth_estate: Clear position. Rare on here.
goth_girls: Brave or bleak? I can’t tell. Both, maybe.
normie_girls: Fair enough. I’m not going to convert you over Hinge.

worldTopics.label: Ask if she wants a family
worldTopics.player: Do you want a family someday?

thunderbirds: Yes, and a nanny, and a house with enough rooms for everyone to avoid each other properly.
I was told for years that a career mattered more. I have the career. I’d trade a chunk of it for a baby, honestly.
police: Someday. When I’ve stopped seeing the worst of what families do to each other.
Yes. Two kids, a dog, and a husband who doesn’t mind me working nights.
progressives: Maybe. I’m not sure it’s responsible to bring kids into a world on fire.
I want one, actually. Which is weirdly controversial in my group chat.
sisters_of_mercy: Yes. As many as God sends. A full table is the best sound in the world.
Very much. A family is the one place you’re loved for being, not doing.
fourth_estate: I keep saying after the next big story. There’s always a next big story.
Yes. I want someone to read the paper to me when I’m old. Even the sports pages.
goth_girls: Surprisingly, yes. A little gothic household. Black cat, tiny children in tiny velvet coats.
I don’t know. I’m scared I’d pass on the sadness. Or the eyeliner.
normie_girls: Yes! Two kids, a garden, and a husband who knows how to use a drill.
One day. My sister has three. She’s exhausted and happier than I’ve ever seen her.

ask: Do you?
What about you? Kids, one day?

stances.label: Say you want kids
stances.player: I do. A house full of them, ideally.

stances.label: Say not yet
stances.player: One day. I’m not ready yet.

stances.label: Say the world’s too dark
stances.player: I’m not sure the world deserves any more children.

thunderbirds: Good. A man with a plan for a dynasty. My mother would approve.
police: That’s a good answer. Steady.
progressives: Okay, but will you do the night feeds? Because that’s the real question.
sisters_of_mercy: Then we want the same thing. That matters more than almost anything.
fourth_estate: Noted, and quietly approved.
goth_girls: A whole house full? Brave. I’ll think about it.
normie_girls: Oh my God, same. Okay, you’re on the shortlist.

thunderbirds: Don’t leave it too long. Ask any of my friends.
police: Fair. No point rushing it.
progressives: Sensible. Better than having them to prove something.
sisters_of_mercy: There’s never a perfect time. But I understand.
fourth_estate: Same. There’s always another deadline.
goth_girls: Mm. The most honest answer there is.
normie_girls: Fair. Don’t wait forever, though!

thunderbirds: How gloomy. The world’s always been dark, darling. People had babies anyway.
police: I see a lot of darkness. I still think kids are the point.
progressives: I’ve thought that too. It’s a hard thing to say out loud.
sisters_of_mercy: Every child is God saying the world should go on. I’m sorry you can’t hear it yet.
fourth_estate: Grim. Not unreasonable. Still grim.
goth_girls: Ha. Finally, someone who reads the news.
normie_girls: Oh. That’s really sad.

worldTopics.label: Ask if phones ruined everyone
worldTopics.player: Do you think phones ruined everyone?

thunderbirds: Dinner parties used to be conversation. Now they’re eight people photographing a risotto.
I gave my nephew a book for his birthday. He asked what it was for.
police: Every crime now has a video and no witnesses. Everyone filmed it. Nobody saw it.
Phones made people braver online and more cowardly everywhere else.
progressives: The apps are built by men in hoodies to keep you anxious and scrolling. That isn’t a moral failing. It’s a business model.
Phones gave a voice to people who never had one. They also gave everyone a megaphone and nobody ears.
sisters_of_mercy: People carry the whole world in their pocket and still can’t sit with themselves for five minutes. Prayer is the opposite of scrolling.
I put mine in a drawer when I pray. The silence frightened me at first. Now it feeds me.
fourth_estate: The phone killed the newspaper and then started printing rumours instead. Guess which one people trust.
Everyone’s a journalist now. Nobody checks anything.
goth_girls: Everyone stares into a little glowing coffin all day. At least mine is honest about it.
People used to write letters and wait. Waiting made things matter.
normie_girls: I check mine about two hundred times a day. Is that bad? Don’t answer.
I deleted the apps once. Lasted three days. Felt amazing. Then I got bored.

question: Are you addicted to yours?
How bad is your screen time?

warm.label: Admit you are
warm.player: Hopelessly. I’m on it right now, talking to you.

challenge.label: Say phones aren’t the problem
challenge.player: Phones aren’t the problem. People were always lonely; now we can see it.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: My phone and I are in a committed relationship. You’re the other woman.

worldTopics.label: Ask about all the therapy talk
worldTopics.player: Everyone talks like a therapist now. Boundaries, trauma, toxic. What do you make of it?

thunderbirds: My friends don’t have problems any more. They have trauma responses. One called being late a trauma response.
My grandmother had a word for most of it. The word was life.
police: I see real trauma at work. When someone calls a rude email trauma, I want to show them a crime scene.
Some people need help, badly. Others just want a word that means not my fault.
progressives: Therapy saved my life. People mock the language because they’re scared of the feelings.
Fine, toxic is overused. But men of my dad’s generation needed some of these words and never had them.
sisters_of_mercy: We used to call it confession. It was free, and it ended with forgiveness. Therapy never quite gets to the forgiveness.
There’s wisdom in it. But the self is a poor god. It can’t absolve you.
fourth_estate: The language spread faster than the help did. Everyone can say boundaries. Not everyone can see a counsellor.
It’s become a way to win arguments. You’re gaslighting me ends a conversation faster than any fact.
goth_girls: Everyone wants a diagnosis like it’s an accessory. I just have a personality.
Pain used to make art. Now it makes captions.
normie_girls: My friend says I have an anxious attachment style. I think I just like texting.
I tried therapy. She was nice. I mostly talked about my mum.

question: Have you ever been to therapy?
Are you a boundaries man?

warm.label: Say it helps people
warm.player: If it helps people, I’m for it.

challenge.label: Say it made everyone fragile
challenge.player: I think it’s made everyone fragile. We used to be told to cope.

joke.label: Make a joke
joke.player: My therapist is Hector. He charges in tacos.

worldTopics.label: Ask what’s happened to men
worldTopics.player: Everyone says men are in crisis. What’s happened to men?

thunderbirds: Men used to build railways. Now they build personal brands. I blame the brands.
My father ran a business and a household and never once said the word self-care. He was miserable, but competent.
police: I arrest a lot of young men with nothing to do and nothing to lose. That isn’t a crisis of masculinity. It’s a crisis of purpose.
Most men I meet are decent and lost. A few are dangerous and very sure of themselves.
progressives: Men aren’t in crisis because women got jobs. They’re in crisis because nobody taught them to do anything but compete.
I feel for them, honestly. The influencers selling them anger are worse than any feminist.
sisters_of_mercy: Men need to be needed. The world told them they weren’t, and many believed it.
A man with a vocation is a happy man. Fatherhood, a craft, the priesthood. Something to give his life to.
fourth_estate: Every paper has run the crisis of men piece. None of them asked men. I did. They said they were lonely.
The numbers are real: fewer degrees, fewer friends, fewer marriages. The explanations are where everyone starts shouting.
goth_girls: Men lost their rituals. No wars, no initiations, no fathers. So they invent fake ones online.

question: Do you care how things look?

worldTopics.player: Can I ask about your last relationship?

Galas are funerals for people who aren’t dead yet.
normie_girls: That’s so scary. She just never came home?

Imagine dressing up that nice and never coming home. It keeps me up at night.

lines: Between us, the treasurer left the gala early and came back without his tie. Nobody’s asked why.
thunderbirds.note: A Bluebird says Treasurer Pell left the gala early and came back without his tie.

lines: Our photographer had a shot of Table 9 that the editor spiked. Make of that what you like.

thunderbirds: Poor Professor Vale. Brakes, then a fire. Somebody up at that university hates good conversation.
He’s speaking at our gala next season, if anyone lets him live that long. That’s not a joke, actually.
Adrian books the most deliciously awful speakers. Someone clearly can’t take a joke.
If you set a man’s house alight over his guest list, darling, you’ve lost the argument.

People keep asking me if it’s connected. I keep not answering.
Two accidents in a row isn’t luck. It’s a pattern with a lawyer.
Somebody wants him scared, not dead. Yet.
progressives: I didn’t want anyone hurt. I wanted him to stop inviting those men. Those aren’t the same thing.

A microphone isn’t a right. But nobody deserved a fire. Both things are true.
Every time something happens to him, we get the blame and he gets a book deal.
sisters_of_mercy: Whatever one thinks of his opinions, nobody deserves fire. We’ve added him to our prayers.
Hatred is a fire too. That’s the part the paper won’t print.
We can disagree with a man and still pray for his safety. That used to be normal.
He invites difficult people to dinner. So did Our Lord. Nobody burned His house down.
fourth_estate: The fire report is vague in all the places it shouldn’t be.
I’ve interviewed him. Arrogant, brilliant and much more frightened than he lets on.
Brakes, then a fire. If there’s a third thing, I want to be standing near it with a notebook.
The university statement was four paragraphs of saying nothing. Impressive, really.
goth_girls: Somebody’s got a grudge with a capital G. Not my scene, but I respect the commitment. Kidding. Mostly.

A man who invites monsters to dinner can’t be shocked when the house catches fire. Still. Rude.
Honestly, it’s nice that somebody on that campus says anything interesting.
normie_girls: Wait, someone’s trying to hurt a professor? Over speeches?
My friend had him for a class. She said he’s mean but funny.
I don’t get why people care so much about who gives a speech.

police: Faith stories are my favourite. Nobody gets arrested.
The chapel ladies are fierce. I wouldn’t cross them.
Church fights are the worst calls. Everyone’s polite and nobody tells the truth.
Give me a bar fight over a parish council any day.

I’m not religious, but I’m on the Sisters’ side. Bishops shouldn’t steamroll people.
Honestly, the guitars are the least of that institution’s problems.
If guitars bring the teenagers in, let them have guitars. Gatekeeping God is wild.
sisters_of_mercy: Guitars at the altar. Next it will be tambourines. We will not have it.
The bishop means well, I think. He just doesn’t understand what the old Mass means to us.
Some things are beautiful because they don’t change. The Latin is one of them.
The bishop means well. So did the man who painted over the frescoes.
fourth_estate: The guitar row is the story that keeps on giving. The letters are wonderful.
Never get between a bishop and a parish. Great copy, though.
The faith pages get more letters than the crime pages. People care about their Mass.
Nobody reads the faith section until a bishop picks a fight. Then everybody does.
goth_girls: Latin and candles beat guitars. I’m with the Sisters on this one, which is a sentence I never expected to say.
Church drama is just goth drama with better architecture.

Church music should sound like a cathedral judging you. Not a campfire.
normie_girls: Guitars at church sounds kind of fun? Don’t tell my nan.

lines: The bishop’s visit is a smokescreen. He wants the chapel land for the developers. Margaret has the letters.

A moonless night is lovely for a garden party. Less so for whatever that crowd is planning.
Goth girls with flyers. My grandmother would have rung the bishop and the papers, in that order.
Somebody tell those girls that black lace isn’t a personality.
police: We’ve had calls about lights at the old chapel. Probably kids. Probably.

Kids with candles in old chapels. Ninety-nine times it’s nothing. I worry about the hundredth.
We get a call about that crowd every week. Never anything we can charge.
progressives: People are panicking about goths again. It’s always the outsiders who get blamed.
There’s something off about that crowd, and I usually defend everyone.
A moral panic about girls in black is a tale as old as time.
If it’s a real threat, investigate it. If it’s eyeliner, leave them alone.
sisters_of_mercy: That old chapel was ours once. Whatever they’re planning there, we’ll be praying against it.
A night with no moon, a gig with no address. I don’t like it.
We will keep the lamps lit in the old chapels. That is what we do.
The young ones come looking for something holy. Some of them find the wrong thing first.
fourth_estate: Somebody slipped a crescent moon into our gig listings. I’m trying to find out who.
The heritage survey on that chapel is three pages of nothing and one page of very strange.
Crescent moons chalked on chapel doors. Do you know how good that looks on a front page?
Every editor wants a cult. Usually it’s a book club with candles.
goth_girls: The gig’s real. The rest of what people are saying… I’d stay home that night.
Every scene has a few people who take the theatre too seriously. That’s all I’ll say.
A crescent on the flyer and no address. That’s how you know it’s the good kind of party.
Victoria’s nights are either magic or a mistake. Sometimes both.
normie_girls: Is it true there’s going to be some spooky thing at the old chapel? I’m not going!
A moonless night sounds romantic. Or terrifying. Both?
My friend got a flyer and said no. Then she couldn’t stop thinking about it.

Civic engagement is lovely in principle and very loud in practice.

police: Protest days are long days. Mostly peaceful. Mostly.
I’ll be on the cordon. Wave, if you’re there.
Twelve hours on a barrier and someone always asks if I’m proud of myself.

Everyone screaming about the future in a town with no shade. Bold.

normie_girls: The traffic was a nightmare because of it, ugh.
It looked kind of exciting on the news, honestly.
I didn’t even know what it was about. Something about a speaker?

lines: Someone photographs every face in the crowd, and it isn’t us.

Horrid. I lock the car twice now.

Crime is dreadful. Has anyone tried simply moving?
police: Can’t comment on an open case. You know that.
The paper gets half of it right. The other half keeps me employed.
The report always reads cleaner than the scene.
Nobody rings us when it goes right. That’s the job.

Someone’s child, every time. Someone’s child.

Why is it always a white van? Is there a white van shop?

normie_girls: Hiii, it’s me! Is this okay? I just wanted to hear your voice.
Okay, I’m calling, which means I like you, which is terrifying. Hi.
Hiii! Sorry, I know, I called, I’m a calling person, deal with it.
Okay, I’m on the bus and the man next to me is eating soup. Distract me.
I just wanted to say hi before my shift. Hi!
Is it bad that I practised what I’d say before I rang? I forgot all of it.

flirt.label: Flirt with her
player: I was hoping it was you.
You have a ridiculously good phone voice.
Funny. I was just thinking about you.

ask.label: Ask what’s new in Sunfall
ask.player: So what’s going on in Sunfall? Tell me everything.

go.label: Say you have to go
go.player: I’d better go, but I’m really glad you called.

thunderbirds: Flattery. Excellent. Keep going; I’ll tell you when to stop. I won’t.
You’d look rather good at a gala. In a proper suit.
Careful. I’m starting to think about seating you next to me.
Careful. Flattery works on me and I hate that it works.
Say that again, slowly. I’m writing it in my diary.
You’re dangerous. My mother would hate you. That’s a compliment.
police: Smooth. I’ve interviewed smoother. Not many.
You’re making it hard to stay professional, and I’m not even at work.
Keep talking like that and I’ll have to investigate you. Thoroughly.
Smooth. I’m going to let that one go with a warning.
You’re lucky I’m off duty.
Keep talking like that and I might actually take a day off.
progressives: Stop it. Okay, don’t stop.
I’m meant to be dismantling the patriarchy and instead I’m blushing.
You’re very charming for a man I suspect of having opinions about Paglia.
Okay, that was objectified, but in a nice way. I’m allowing it.
Stop. I’m blushing and I had a whole argument planned.
That’s really sweet. Annoyingly sweet.
sisters_of_mercy: Oh. You’re kind. I’m blushing, and there’s nobody here to see.
That’s a lovely thing to say.
Careful. I might believe you.
Oh. That’s very kind. I’m blushing, and nobody is here to see it.
You shouldn’t say things like that. Say them again, though.
My aunt would say you’re a charmer. She’d be right.
fourth_estate: Is that on the record? I want it on the record.
Careful. I write things down.
Best quote I’ve had in days.
That’s going in my notes. Under evidence he likes me.
Quotable. I’m keeping that one.
You’re very good at this. Off the record, it’s working.
goth_girls: Mm. Say that again, slower.
You’re dangerous. I like dangerous.
Keep talking. Your voice beats my records.
Ugh. That was actually romantic. Gross. Do it again.
You’re going to make me smile in public and ruin my whole look.
That was dark enough to be sincere. I approve.
normie_girls: Oh my God, stop, I’m smiling like an idiot.
Okay, you’re really good at this. Suspiciously good.
I’m literally kicking my feet right now.
Okay stop, I’m actually blushing, my roommate is laughing at me.
You’re so cheesy. I love it.
I’m screenshotting this call in my brain.

thunderbirds.line: Between us, Dorian Kell has been very quiet since the gala. Dorian is never quiet.
thunderbirds.note: A Bluebird says Dorian Kell has gone unusually quiet since the gala.

thunderbirds.line: The foundation hired a new accountant straight after the gala. Nobody voted on it.
thunderbirds.note: A Bluebird says the foundation hired a new accountant after the gala without a vote.

thunderbirds.line: Professor Vale is invited to our next dinner. Half the committee wants him there; the other half wants police at the door.
thunderbirds.note: Professor Vale is invited to a Bluebirds dinner, and half the committee wants police there.

police.line: Off the record: that grey sedan people keep reporting? It’s registered to a company that doesn’t exist.
police.note: A police officer says the grey sedan is registered to a company that doesn’t exist.

police.line: We’ve had three complaints about lights in the old chapel at night. Nobody wants to go out there.
police.note: Police have had complaints about lights in the old chapel at night.

police.line: If you ever need us, don’t text. Ring 911, say exactly where you are, then stay put.
police.note: A police officer says to ring 911 and stay put if you’re ever in danger.

progressives.line: The Back Row people asked me for a meeting room. No name, no agenda. I said no.
progressives.note: A Progressive says the Back Row asked for a meeting room with no name and no agenda.

progressives.line: Someone on campus is passing round Vale’s timetable to anyone who asks. That can’t be good.
progressives.note: Someone on campus is passing round Professor Vale’s timetable.

progressives.line: The housing office keeps losing complaints from the motel strip. I’m keeping copies.
progressives.note: A Progressive is keeping copies of housing complaints the university keeps losing.

sisters_of_mercy.line: The bell tower at St Brigid’s has a new lock, and nobody in the parish has a key.
sisters_of_mercy.note: A Sister says the bell tower at St Brigid’s has a new lock nobody in the parish holds a key to.

fourth_estate.line: The editor killed my piece on the gala seating plan. Someone rang him first. I want to know who.
fourth_estate.note: A reporter says her piece on the gala seating plan was killed after someone rang the editor.

fourth_estate.line: Our photographer saw someone in a black veil leaving the old chapel before dawn.
fourth_estate.note: A photographer saw someone in a black veil leaving the old chapel before dawn.

fourth_estate.line: Vale’s research assistant has cancelled two interviews with me. Nervous people cancel interviews.
fourth_estate.note: Professor Vale’s research assistant keeps cancelling interviews.

goth_girls.line: Victoria’s asked everyone to keep the moonless night free. Don’t ask what for. I didn’t.
goth_girls.note: Victoria Blackwood wants everyone free on the moonless night.

goth_girls.line: Someone painted a crescent inside the old chapel’s bell tower. It wasn’t there before.
goth_girls.note: Someone has painted a crescent inside the old chapel’s bell tower.

goth_girls.line: If you ever find a pendant on your doorstep, don’t pick it up with bare hands. Just a feeling.
goth_girls.note: A goth warns: never pick up a pendant left on your doorstep with bare hands.

normie_girls.line: My cousin works nights at the motel. She says a man in a charity lanyard paid cash for a room the night of the gala.
normie_girls.note: A man in a charity lanyard paid cash for a motel room on the night of the gala.

normie_girls.line: Hector at the taco stand says the bear only comes on nights the bins go out. Hector knows everything.
normie_girls.note: Hector at the taco stand says the bear comes on nights the bins go out.

normie_girls.line: Someone keeps leaving flowers at the old interstate junction. Nobody knows who.
normie_girls.note: Someone keeps leaving flowers at the old interstate junction.

noTell: Honestly? Nothing new. Sunfall is being suspiciously normal.
Nothing worth repeating. I’ll find you some gossip for next time.
It’s quiet. Too quiet. Ask me tomorrow.
I have nothing. I spent the day watching a pigeon fight a crisp packet.
No gossip. I’ve been a model citizen. It’s exhausting.
Honestly, the most interesting thing that happened was a new flavour of crisps.
Nothing. Sunfall is holding its breath.
I heard nothing, which is suspicious in itself.

thunderbirds: I must dash. Dream of me, darling. That’s an instruction.
Right, the committee calls. Goodbye, you.
My car’s here. Behave, if you can.
I’m being summoned. Be fascinating tomorrow.
police: Break’s over. Stay out of trouble. I mean it.
Got to go. Lock your door tonight, okay?
Radio’s going. I’m off. Stay sharp.
Got a call coming in. Take care of yourself.
progressives: Okay, I have to go and save the world. Or at least the minutes. Bye!
I should go. This was nice. Really nice.
I have a meeting about a meeting. Pray for me. Metaphorically.
Okay, I really have to go. This was a good call.
sisters_of_mercy: I should go. God bless you.
Thank you for talking with me. Sleep well.
The bell’s ringing for vespers. I’ll keep you in my prayers.
I must go and help with supper. Goodnight.
fourth_estate: Deadline. I have to go. Don’t do anything I’d have to report.
I’ll let you go. Off the record: I smiled the whole time.
My editor is glaring at me. Bye for now.
That’s my cue. Talk soon, source.
goth_girls: I’m going now. Think of me when it gets dark.
Bye. Don’t let the bear in. Or do. Your call.
The candles are burning low. That means goodbye.
I’m hanging up now. Dramatically.
normie_girls: Okay, I’ll let you go. Text me later? Bye bye bye.
Bye! This made my whole day.
Okay, my food’s here. Bye! Talk later!
I have to go but this was so nice. Bye!

thunderbirds: I rang. You didn’t answer. I’ll forgive you, eventually.
Missed you. I don’t ring twice, darling. Usually.
I rang. You were elsewhere. How intriguing.
A missed call from me is a privilege. Return it.
police: Tried to call. All good? Just checking.
Called you. No answer. Should I be worried?
Missed call. Ring back when you can.
Tried you. Not worried. Mostly.
progressives: I called and you didn’t pick up and now I feel insane for calling. Cool.
I was brave and called! You weren’t there. Typical.
Called. No answer. Respecting your boundaries. Ring me back though.
Okay, I called, it went to voicemail, I panicked and hung up.
sisters_of_mercy: I tried to ring you. I’ll try another time. God bless.
I rang, but you must have been busy. I hope all is well.
I tried to call. I hope you’re resting.
I rang to say good evening. Good evening.
fourth_estate: Called. Voicemail. Noted.
Tried you. Missed you. Story of my life.
Unreturned call logged. You know I keep records.
Tried you. I’ll try again. I always do.
goth_girls: I called. You didn’t answer. Mysterious. I approve.
Missed call from me. Treasure it.
I called into the void. The void didn’t answer.
You missed my call. It was going to be poetic.
normie_girls: Called you!! You missed it 😭
I rang you but you were busy, I guess. Next time!
Called but you’re busy!! Call me back!
I called you and then got shy and hung up. Hi.

open: Hello. I hope it’s all right that I rang. There’s something I’d like to ask you. It matters to me.
It’s me. I’ve been praying about you, and I wanted to hear your voice. May I ask you something?
Good evening. I hope I’m not interrupting. I want to know you better, properly. Can I ask you a question?
examIntro: If you’re serious about me, you should know the faith. Here’s one:
My father would ask you this, so I will:
Forgive me, it’s a small test:
right: That’s right. You’ve been reading. I’m very glad.
Correct. My aunt would be impressed. I am too.
Yes. Oh, that makes me happier than it should.
wrong: Not quite. It was {answer}. Don’t worry. You’ll learn.
No, it was {answer}. I’ll be patient with you.
That’s not it. The answer is {answer}. We’ll study together.

asks.ask: Would you want to marry in the old rite, in the chapel?

answers.label: Say yes, the old rite
answers.player: Yes. The old rite, in the chapel. Properly.
answers.pos: Then we want the same wedding.

answers.label: Say it’s up to her
answers.player: Wherever you want. It’s your day.
answers.pos: That’s sweet. It’s our day, though.
answers.neg: It isn’t only my day. It’s a sacrament.

answers.label: Say a registry office
answers.player: Honestly, a registry office would be fine for me.
answers.pos: Hm. We’d have to talk about that.
answers.neg: That would be very hard for me.

asks.ask: If God sent us children, would you want them raised in the faith?

answers.label: Say yes, in the faith
answers.player: Yes. Baptised, taught, brought to Mass.
answers.pos: Thank you. That’s everything to me.

answers.label: Say let them choose
answers.player: I’d let them choose for themselves when they’re older.
answers.pos: Hm. Children can’t choose what they’ve never been given.
answers.neg: Children can’t choose what they’ve never been given.

answers.label: Say you’d learn alongside them
answers.player: I’d want to learn it with them. I’m still learning myself.
answers.neg: Learning is good. Doing is better.

asks.ask: Some people say a husband should lead his family. What do you think?

answers.label: Say you’d lead, gently
answers.player: I’d lead. Gently, and by serving first.
answers.pos: That’s what headship means. You understand it.

answers.label: Say it should be equal
answers.player: I think it should be fifty-fifty, on everything.
answers.pos: Equal in dignity, yes. Different in calling.
answers.neg: We’d have to talk about that.

answers.label: Say you’d decide together
answers.player: I’d want us to decide things together, and pray about the hard ones.
answers.neg: Together is good. Someone still has to carry it.

asks.ask: Would you come to Mass with me? Every week, not only for weddings and funerals?

answers.label: Say yes, every week
answers.player: Every week. I’d like that.
answers.neg: Every week is a promise. Keep it.

answers.label: Say you’ll try
answers.player: I’ll try. I’m not there yet, but I want to be.

answers.label: Say it’s not for you
answers.player: Honestly? Church isn’t for me.
answers.neg: Then I don’t know how this works.

bye: I should go. God bless you. I’ll pray for you tonight.
Thank you for talking with me. Sleep well, and say your prayers.
I must go. This was good. Truly.

twoTruths.label: Play two truths and a lie
twoTruths.player: Let’s play two truths and a lie. You first.
intro: Okay. Two truths and a lie. Ready?
Fine, but I’m very good at this.
Oh, I love this game. Brace yourself.
right: Ugh. Correct. How did you know?
Correct. Now I’m slightly scared of you.
Yes. That one was the lie. I’m impressed.
wrong: Wrong! The lie was the {lie} one.
Nope. It was number {lie}. You don’t know me as well as you think.
Ha! It was the {lie} one. I’m a better liar than you thought.
