arcs.hook: My little sister just got engaged. To Darren. I can’t stand Darren. And I have to give a speech.

ask.label: Ask what’s wrong with Darren
ask.player: What’s actually wrong with Darren?
ask.reply: He calls her babe in front of our nan and he has never once asked her a question about herself. She’s happy, though. Do I say something, or smile and give the speech?

choices.label: Tell her to talk to her sister first
choices.player: Talk to your sister. Privately. Before the speech.
choices.now: Yeah. You’re right. I’ll take her for a drink.
choices.next: I talked to her. She cried, I cried, then she said Darren is the only man who has ever stayed. I’m giving the speech. I’m going to be nice.

choices.label: Tell her to smile and give the speech
choices.player: Smile, give the speech, and love her anyway.
choices.now: That’s probably the grown-up answer. I hate it.
choices.next: The speech went fine. Darren cried. Maybe he’s alright. Don’t tell anyone I said that.

news.title: ENGAGEMENT PARTY TAKES OVER THE LUCKY CACTUS
news.summary: The bride’s sister kept her speech short and kind.
news.body: A Sunfall couple celebrated their engagement at the Lucky Cactus. {name}, the bride’s sister, gave a short speech that made the groom cry.

choices.label: Tell her to roast Darren in the speech
choices.player: Roast him. Lovingly. Mostly.
choices.next: I roasted Darren. Nobody laughed except Darren. My sister isn’t speaking to me. Thanks for that.

payoff.line: My sister asked about you, by the way. I said you gave me good advice. Don’t let it go to your head.

item.label: A slice of engagement cake
item.text: Wrapped in a napkin, with a note from {first}: for luck. Darren made it. It’s actually good.

arcs.hook: Sorry if I’m slow replying. My dad’s in hospital. It’s his heart. He says he’s fine. He always says he’s fine.

ask.label: Ask how her dad really is
ask.player: How is your dad doing, honestly?
ask.reply: Grumpy, which is a good sign. Mum wants me to move back home to help. I’d have to give up my flat. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to go home for a while
choices.player: Go home for a bit. Flats come back. Dads don’t.
choices.now: Yeah. I know. I just needed someone to say it.
choices.next: I’m back in my old bedroom. There’s a poster of a boy band on the wall. Dad’s already bossing me about. It’s nice.

choices.label: Tell her to keep her flat and visit
choices.player: Keep your flat. Visit every day you can.
choices.now: That’s what I want to do. Is that selfish?
choices.next: I’ve been going straight from work every day. He pretends he’s annoyed. Thank you for not making me feel guilty.

choices.label: Tell her he’ll be fine
choices.player: He’ll be fine. They always are.
choices.next: He’s home now. You were right, I suppose. You didn’t have to sound so sure about it, though.

payoff.line: Dad asked who I keep texting. I said a friend. He said friends don’t make you smile like that. Mortifying.

item.label: A get-well card
item.text: Signed by her dad, for some reason: Thanks for looking after my girl. Grumpily, Dad.

arcs.hook: My mum has set me up with three men from her church this week. Three. One of them brought a briefcase.

ask.label: Ask about the man with the briefcase
ask.player: Who brings a briefcase to a set-up?
ask.reply: An accountant called Graham. He was nice! That’s the problem. She wants me to see him again. How do I get out of it?

choices.label: Tell her to be honest with her mum
choices.player: Tell your mum the truth: you’ll find your own man.
choices.now: She’ll cry. Then she’ll make soup. Okay.
choices.next: I told her. She cried, made soup, then asked if the man I’m talking to has a job. I said yes. You do, don’t you?

choices.label: Tell her to mention you
choices.player: Tell her you’re talking to someone.
choices.next: I told Mum about you. She wants your star sign and your intentions. I said Hinge. She said what’s Hinge. It went downhill from there.

choices.label: Tell her to give Graham a chance
choices.player: Give Graham a chance. Briefcases are underrated.
choices.next: I went out with Graham again. He’s lovely. We’re seeing each other, so this is goodbye. Thank you, I suppose.

payoff.line: Mum’s stopped setting me up. She says she’s waiting to meet you. No pressure. Lots of pressure.

arcs.hook: My little brother owes money to some men from the motel on the interstate. He won’t say how much.

ask.label: Ask what kind of men
ask.player: What kind of men are we talking about?
ask.reply: The kind who park outside and don’t get out of the car. He wants me to lend it to him. I have it, just about. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to pay it, once
choices.player: Pay it once. Make him promise it’s the last time.
choices.next: I paid. The car outside has gone. He hugged me for the first time since he was twelve.

choices.label: Tell her to ring the police
choices.player: Ring the police. Let them deal with the car.
choices.now: He’ll never forgive me. But okay.
choices.next: The police went to the motel. My brother is furious with me. He’ll be fine. He’ll be alive, anyway.

news.title: TWO MEN QUESTIONED AFTER MOTEL TIP-OFF
news.summary: Police thank a member of the public.
news.body: Officers questioned two men at the interstate motel after a tip-off about threats over a debt. A young man and his sister have been offered help.

choices.label: Tell her to let him learn
choices.player: Let him sort it out. He has to learn.
choices.next: He turned up with a black eye. He says he walked into a door. I keep thinking about what you said.

payoff.line: My brother wants to buy you a drink. He thinks you’re the reason I didn’t kill him. Don’t go. He’ll make you pay.

arcs.hook: My boss presented my idea at a meeting today. My idea. My slides. He said we.

ask.label: Ask what she’s going to do
ask.player: So what are you going to do about it?
ask.reply: Nothing, probably. That’s the problem. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to tell him, calmly
choices.player: Tell him, calmly, that it was your idea.
choices.now: Calmly. I can do calmly. Probably.
choices.next: I told him. He said he was sure he’d mentioned me. Then he gave me the next project with my name on it. I nearly fainted.

choices.label: Tell her to go over his head
choices.player: Go to his boss. Take the files.
choices.next: I went to his boss. Now I have his job. He has the desk by the printer. I feel slightly bad. Slightly.

news.title: SUNFALL FIRM NAMES NEW TEAM LEADER
news.summary: A promotion from within, after a disputed presentation.
news.body: {name} has been promoted to lead her team. Colleagues say she has been doing the job for a while anyway.

choices.label: Tell her to quit
choices.player: Quit. They don’t deserve you.
choices.next: I quit. Mum isn’t speaking to me. I’m eating cereal for dinner. I hope you’re happy.

payoff.line: I got a bonus. I’m not saying it was because of you. I’m not not saying it.

item.label: A fancy pen
item.text: Engraved with her firm’s name. She says she has a drawer full of them and you deserve one.

arcs.hook: I’ve been looking at an empty shop on Main Street for a month. I want to open my own place. Don’t laugh.

ask.label: Ask what she’d open
ask.player: What would you open?
ask.reply: A tiny café that does one thing really well. Cinnamon buns. I’ve saved enough for three months, then nothing. Should I?

choices.label: Tell her to go for it
choices.player: Do it. Three months is plenty to prove it.
choices.next: I signed the lease. I’m terrified. Come and be my first customer. Well, you can’t. You know what I mean.

news.title: NEW CAFÉ ON MAIN STREET SELLS ONE THING
news.summary: Cinnamon buns. That’s it. The queue went round the corner.
news.body: {name} has opened a tiny café on Main Street that sells only cinnamon buns. The queue went round the corner by lunchtime.

choices.label: Tell her to wait and save
choices.player: Wait a year. Save more. Then do it.
choices.next: Someone else took the shop. It’s a vape shop now. I walk past it every day. I’m fine.

choices.label: Tell her to try a market stall first
choices.player: Try a market stall first and see.
choices.now: Ooh. Low risk. I like that.
choices.next: I did a stall at the market. Sold out in two hours. I’m doing it again. Then maybe the shop.

item.label: A cinnamon bun
item.text: Wrapped in brown paper, from her market stall. Still slightly warm.

payoff.line: I named a bun after you. It’s the plain one. Joking. It’s the best one.

arcs.hook: My ex messaged me last night. First time in a year. He wants to talk.

ask.label: Ask what she wants to do
ask.player: What do you want to do about him?
ask.reply: I don’t know. He was my whole life for three years. Then he wasn’t. What would you say, if you were me?

choices.label: Tell her to give him another chance
choices.player: Give him a chance. People change.
choices.next: I met him. He has changed. We’re going to try again. You were really kind about it. Bye, then.

choices.label: Tell her she deserves better
choices.player: You deserve someone who never left.
choices.now: That’s quite a line. It worked, though.
choices.next: I told him no. It felt amazing. I deleted his number and ate a whole pizza.

choices.label: Ask what she actually wants
choices.player: What do you want? Not him. You.
choices.now: Nobody’s asked me that in ages.
choices.next: I thought about what you asked. I want a dog and a quiet life and someone who asks me things. So. No to him.

payoff.line: My ex saw I was happy and messaged again. I didn’t reply. I was too busy talking to you.

arcs.hook: My best friend and I aren’t speaking. Twelve years, and now nothing, over a birthday.

ask.label: Ask what happened
ask.player: What happened with your best friend?
ask.reply: I forgot her birthday. Completely. She found out I’d been out that night from someone’s photos. Do I grovel, or wait for her to calm down?

choices.label: Tell her to grovel, with cake
choices.player: Grovel. With cake.
choices.next: I turned up with a cake and cried on her doorstep. We’re fine. She wants to meet you, by the way. She’s on Hinge. Be nice.

choices.label: Tell her to give it a week
choices.player: Give it a week. She’ll miss you.
choices.next: She messaged first. She said she missed me. You were right, annoyingly.

choices.label: Say her friend is overreacting
choices.player: Honestly, she’s overreacting.
choices.next: I told her what you said. Now neither of them is speaking to me, and I’m not speaking to you.

payoff.line: My best friend approves of you. That has never happened. Not once.

arcs.hook: Can I tell you something embarrassing? I write songs. Nobody knows.

ask.label: Ask what her songs are about
ask.player: What are your songs about?
ask.reply: Mostly men who didn’t text back. There’s an open mic at the Lucky Cactus. Should I do it?

choices.label: Tell her to do the open mic
choices.player: Do it. I’ll be cheering from here.
choices.now: From your bedroom. Very supportive. Okay.
choices.next: I did it. My voice shook for the first song and not the second. A man at the bar bought me a drink. I wish it had been you.

news.title: SURPRISE STAR AT LUCKY CACTUS OPEN MIC
news.summary: A first-timer brought the room to silence.
news.body: {name} played her own songs at the Lucky Cactus open mic for the first time. The regulars have asked her to come back.

choices.label: Tell her to record one first
choices.player: Record one first, just for you.
choices.now: Baby steps. I can do baby steps.
choices.next: I recorded one. I’ve listened to it forty times. It’s about you a bit. Don’t ask which bit.

item.label: A burned CD
item.text: One song on it, and her handwriting on the label: not about you. It is.

choices.label: Ask if any are about you
choices.player: Are any of them about me?
choices.next: I’m not telling you about my songs any more.

payoff.line: I played my new song for my mum. She cried. She asked who it was for. I said a man who listens.

arcs.hook: I got offered a job. A good one. In another city.

ask.label: Ask about the job
ask.player: Tell me about the job.
ask.reply: Double the money, half the sun, nobody I know. I have to answer soon. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to take it
choices.player: Take it. You can always come back.
choices.now: You’re right. I hate that you’re right.
choices.next: I took it. I leave soon. Thank you for being honest with me. I’ll miss this.

choices.label: Tell her to stay
choices.player: Stay. Sunfall needs you.

choices.next: I said no. My boss gave me a raise to stop me leaving. I should have asked for more.

choices.label: Ask her to stay for you
choices.player: Stay for me.
choices.now: We met on an app about a week ago.
choices.next: I’m staying. Not for you. For the sun. It was a nice thing to say. Weird, but nice.

payoff.line: I keep the job offer in a drawer. I look at it when work is bad. Then I look at my phone instead.

item.label: A postcard
item.text: Blank, from the city she nearly moved to. She kept it to remind her why she stayed.

arcs.hook: My landlord is putting my rent up again. I can’t afford it. I might have to move.

ask.label: Ask what she’ll do about the rent
ask.player: What are you going to do about the rent?
ask.reply: Fight him, take a second job, or move in with my friend who has four cats. Pick one.

choices.label: Tell her to fight it
choices.player: Fight it. Look up your rights.
choices.next: I wrote him a letter with lots of long words. He backed down. I’m drunk on power.

choices.label: Tell her to take a second job
choices.player: Take a second job for a bit.
choices.next: I’m working nights at the diner now. I’m so tired I called my boss Mum.

item.label: A diner napkin
item.text: With a doodle of you on it, by her. Not a flattering doodle.

choices.label: Tell her to move in with the cats
choices.player: Four cats? That sounds like a home.
choices.next: I moved in. One of the cats sleeps on my face. I think I’ve never been happier.

payoff.line: I paid my rent today and didn’t cry. Growth. Thank you for listening to me moan.

arcs.hook: My gran died. It was expected. It still feels like the floor has gone.

ask.label: Ask about her gran
ask.player: Tell me about your gran.
ask.reply: She taught me to make bread and to swear in two languages. We’re clearing her house. Do I keep her things, or let my aunts have them?

choices.label: Tell her to keep one small thing
choices.player: Keep one small thing. Something she used every day.
choices.now: Her wooden spoon. She hit us with it. Lovingly.
choices.next: I kept the spoon. It’s on my kitchen wall. I say good morning to it.

item.label: Her gran’s bread recipe
item.text: Copied out by {first} from the original card. At the bottom, in her gran’s words: don’t rush it.

choices.label: Tell her to fight for it all
choices.player: Fight for it. You were closest to her.
choices.next: I fought my aunts over a teapot. Nobody won. We all eat separately at family dinners now.

choices.label: Just listen
choices.player: I’m sorry. Tell me more about her.
choices.now: She once threw a shoe at a man who was rude to a waitress. She was eighty.
choices.next: Thank you for listening. I didn’t need advice. I needed that.

payoff.line: I made Gran’s bread for the first time. It was terrible. She’d have laughed. I laughed.

arcs.hook: Can I be honest with you? I’ve been finding it hard to pray lately. That has never happened to me before.

ask.label: Ask what has changed
ask.player: What has changed, do you think?
ask.reply: Nothing. That’s the hard part. The words are the same and they feel far away. What would you do?

choices.label: Offer to pray with her
choices.player: Would it help if I prayed with you? Even from here.
choices.now: That’s the kindest thing anyone has said to me in a long time.
choices.next: I went to the early Mass and the words came back. I thought of you, a little. I hope that isn’t wrong.

choices.label: Tell her the saints had dry spells too
choices.player: Doubt is part of faith. Even the saints had dry spells.
choices.now: Mother Teresa did. I’d forgotten that.
choices.next: I read about the saints and their dry spells. It helped. Thank you for knowing that.

item.label: A holy card
item.text: Saint Thérèse, a little worn. On the back: thank you for being patient with me.

choices.label: Ask if she has ever wondered if it’s real
choices.player: Have you ever wondered if any of it is real?
choices.next: I don’t think we should talk about my faith any more.

payoff.line: Father asked me why I seem lighter lately. I said a friend was praying for me. He said keep that friend.

arcs.hook: My roommate ate my food again. I labelled it. With my name. She ate it anyway.

ask.label: Ask what she ate
ask.player: What did she eat?
ask.reply: A whole lasagne. It took me two hours. Do I say something, or do I hide the next one in my wardrobe?

choices.label: Tell her to talk to her roommate
choices.player: Talk to her. Kindly. Then buy a lock.
choices.now: A lock. On a fridge. Yes.
choices.next: We talked. She’s broke and she’s been skipping meals. I make two lasagnes now.

choices.label: Tell her to eat the roommate’s food
choices.player: Eat her food. Fair’s fair.
choices.next: I ate her yoghurts. She ate my birthday cake. It’s war now. Thanks.

choices.label: Tell her to move out
choices.player: Life’s too short for lasagne thieves. Move.
choices.next: I didn’t move out. I did tell her you said I should. She thinks you’re dramatic.

payoff.line: I made you a lasagne. Well, a portion. It’s in my fridge with your name on it. Nobody will eat this one.

item.label: A tub of lasagne
item.text: With your name on the lid in marker pen. She says nobody will dare.

arcs.hook: I’ve been thinking about going back to study. I left school at sixteen. Is that stupid?

ask.label: Ask what she’d study
ask.player: What would you study?
ask.reply: Nursing. Or law. Something where people listen when I speak. I’d be the oldest there by years. Should I?

choices.label: Tell her to enrol
choices.player: Enrol. Being the oldest just means you know why you’re there.
choices.now: Okay. I’m filling in the form now. Don’t watch.
choices.next: I enrolled. I bought new pencils like a child. I’m so happy.

news.title: SUNFALL COLLEGE SEES MORE ADULT STUDENTS
news.summary: Older students are going back to class.
news.body: Among the new students at Sunfall College is {name}, who left school at sixteen. She says she is tired of being clever in private.

choices.label: Suggest a course online first
choices.player: Try a course online first.

choices.label: Ask why now
choices.player: Why now?
choices.now: Because I’m tired of being clever in private.
choices.next: I thought about what you asked. I’m doing it.

payoff.line: I got my first mark back. A good one. I wanted to tell someone, and it was you.

item.label: A gold star sticker
item.text: From her first marked assignment. She says you can have it. She has more.

arcs.hook: I have to speak in front of the whole company soon. I think I’m going to be sick.

ask.label: Ask what she’s presenting

choices.label: Tell her to tell it straight

choices.label: Tell her to open with a joke
choices.player: Open with a joke. Break the ice.

choices.label: Tell her to call in sick
choices.player: Call in sick.
choices.next: I didn’t call in sick. It was awful and fine. You were no help at all, but thanks for answering.

payoff.line: They want me to do the next one too. Apparently I’m good at bad news.

item.label: A conference lanyard
item.text: With her name on it. She says it’s a trophy now.

ask.reply: Keep an eye out. Tell me if you see anything. Anything at all.

tell.reply: BISCUIT! Oh my God. I’m ringing them now. I could kiss you. I might.

news.title: DOG REUNITED WITH OWNER
news.summary: Biscuit is home, and not sorry.
news.body: A small grey dog found near the Lucky Cactus is home with {name}. She thanked a friend who spotted the advert.

payoff.line: Biscuit sends his love. He has eaten a sock.

item.text: Small, grey, an idiot. Signed with a paw print in what is probably jam.

item.text: From Sunfall Animal Rescue. She says it makes you an honorary dog person.

item.text: Hand-drawn. She knows you can’t come. She wanted you to have one.
